correctness.rationale: L(V) comprises convex and union-closed properties P⊆2^V including empty property and empty team, finite |V|=n>=1. Every proper P omitting the empty team lies below C*=all nonempty teams. Otherwise union of all member teams U belongs to P; U=V would imply P=2^V by convexity, so a valuation v∉U yields P⊆C_v=2^(V\{v}). These n+1 proper P are coatoms, as adjoining a missing team forces the top by union closure and convexity. Coatom-cone covers of the proper part have contractible nonempty intersections, and all nonempty selections of coatoms intersect except the set of all n+1; nerve is boundary of n-simplex, giving homotopy S^(n-1) and Möbius (-1)^(n-1). For k>=1 propositional letters, n=2^k, Möbius -1 using independently cited finite expressive completeness. Independent exhaustive n=1,2,3 property enumerations give 4,11,42 elements and exactly 2,3,4 coatoms. Proof is for arbitrary finite n; not extrapolated from finite tests.
